transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right, and I really don't want to sound difficult or anything. I'm just here because things have been really overwhelming lately, and I want to make sure I'm handling it the right way. 

It’s... well, it’s about my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just standard paperwork and missed payments, you know? Like it's just a normal financial thing. But I... I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even some of the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I know how that probably sounds to someone on the outside, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing going on for almost two years now. I just really needed to talk to someone about it... does that make sense?
Do you think other people, besides those involved with your house, are against you or plotting something?

Oh, no, no... definitely not. I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm, um, like... paranoid about everybody or something. Because I'm not, I promise. 

It's really just... just the people directly tied to the house and my loan. Everyone else in my life is completely fine. My friends, my family, the regular customers at my store... they're all great. I try really hard to get along with everyone, and I usually do. I just... I know how this one specific situation with the bank looks, and I really don't want you to think I'm just pointing fingers at the whole world. 

Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making myself sound... well, worse than I am.
How long have you believed that the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are working together against you?

Um... well, I guess it's been... about a year and nine months? Give or take a little. It really started when the, um, the foreclosure notices and all those constant bank calls just started taking over our home life. 

I really hope I'm not making it sound like I just woke up one day and decided to be difficult or suspicious of people. It wasn't like that at all, I promise. It was just... noticing things over time, with the calls and the paperwork, and how certain things at work were happening at the exact same time. 

Is that... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so I'm not wasting your time.
Do you believe that things you see or hear in your daily life, such as news reports or conversations between others, are somehow related to your situation with the bank and your house?

Um... no, no, not at all. I don't think the news or, like, random people talking at the grocery store have anything to do with me. I really hope I haven't made it sound like I think the whole world is revolving around my house problems. 

I know sometimes people can get really... swept up in things and start seeing connections everywhere, but I promise I'm not like that. It's strictly just the bank, the loan people, and those few at work. I don't watch the news and think they're talking to me or anything like that. 

Does that make sense? I just really want to be clear that I'm keeping a level head about everything else. I'm trying my best to handle this the right way.
Have you ever considered the possibility that the bank and loan servicer are not working together against you, and that the foreclosure is simply a result of missed payments?

I mean... I really have tried to look at it that way. I know that's what everyone else thinks, and I really don't want to sound stubborn or difficult. Everyone keeps acting like, you know, this foreclosure is just standard paperwork and... and missed payments. And I promise you, I have looked at all the papers they've shown me. I really try to be objective about it.

But... um... I just can't ignore what I've been seeing for almost two years now. Even though I want to just accept the simple explanation, I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and even those people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I really hope you don't think I'm just ignoring reality or being unreasonable. It's just that no amount of papers they show me changes what I've actually experienced and seen happening behind the scenes. 

Does that make sense? I really am trying my best to look at this logically, I just want to be honest with you about what's actually going on.
Do you ever have any doubts about your belief that the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are working together against you?

Um... I really wish I could say yes. I know that telling you I have doubts would probably make me sound a lot more... reasonable? And I really, really don't want to come across as stubborn or like I'm refusing to listen to you. I hate feeling like I'm being difficult. 

But... well, kind of like I was just saying, I know everyone else keeps acting like this is all just standard paperwork and missed payments. And I've tried to second-guess myself, I promise I have. But I just know that they've been quietly working together to push me out of my house. No amount of papers they try to show me can change what I've been seeing for almost two years now. 

So... no, I guess I don't really have any doubts anymore, even though part of me wishes I did so this could all just be a big misunderstanding. I'm sorry if that's not what I'm supposed to say, I just... I want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you so you can help me. Is it okay that I'm just laying it all out like that?
Have you changed your behavior in any way because of what you believe is happening with the bank and your house?

Um... well, I really try hard not to let it change how I act. I'm still going to work every day and doing my best as a supervisor. I really pride myself on being reliable, you know? 

But... I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, things at home have gotten a little tense lately. My husband and I, we just... whenever the foreclosure comes up, it kind of turns into an argument. I hate fighting with him, I really do. I don't want you to think we have a bad marriage or anything! It's just... it's a lot of pressure on us right now. 

And... um... at work, I guess I've had a few... tense exchanges with my managers? Just over ordinary paperwork, really. I just feel like I have to be so careful about what I sign or agree to now, given everything else that's going on. I think people have noticed I'm a little on edge, because they're definitely a lot more careful around me now. They kind of tiptoe, which makes me feel awful. 

I'm still working hard and holding it together, though, I promise. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm falling apart or being a difficult person to work with. I'm just trying to protect myself and do the right thing. Is it understandable that I'd be a little stressed out and reacting like that?
Do you think that people are talking about you or your situation when you're not around?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try not to worry about what other people might be saying behind my back. I know that can make a person sound kind of... paranoid, I guess? And I really don't want to come across like that. 

I know people at work are tiptoeing around me a bit, like I mentioned, but I don't think they're having secret meetings about me or anything like that. And my husband and I argue, but I don't think he's going around talking about me to other people. I just... I try to focus on what's right in front of me, you know? The paperwork, the bank... the things I can actually see happening. 

I hope that's the right answer. I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the facts and not blowing things out of proportion. Does that make sense?
How much time do you spend thinking about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working together against you on an average day?

Um... well, I try really hard not to let it consume my whole day. I know that dwelling on things isn't healthy, and I really want to be productive and focused, especially at work. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over this all the time, because I'm definitely not. 

But... I guess it does cross my mind... a fair amount. It's hard not to think about it when I'm dealing with paperwork at work, or when the mail comes at home. I try to push it out of my head and just focus on my job or my husband, but... it's kind of like a low-level hum in the background a lot of the time. 

I'd say... maybe I think about it for a few hours a day, scattered here and there? I really try to keep it contained, though. I hope that doesn't sound like too much. I'm really trying my best to manage it all and stay positive. Is it normal to have it on my mind that much, given the situation?
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working together against you when you're trying to focus on other things?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try very hard to stay focused on whatever task is in front of me, especially when I'm at work. I know how important it is to be present and do a good job, and I really pride myself on being a good supervisor. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting there staring into space or getting distracted when I'm supposed to be helping customers or managing my team.

Sometimes, if I'm doing something quiet, like filing or... or just driving home, it might pop into my head. But I can usually just tell myself, "Okay, put that away for now," and move on to something else. I really try to be disciplined about it. 

I mean, it takes a little effort sometimes, just because the situation with the house is so stressful, but I definitely wouldn't say it's difficult to stop thinking about it. I'm still very much in control of my thoughts. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you know I'm handling things okay.
Have you ever considered that you might be mistaken about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working together against you?

Um... well, I really do try to keep an open mind. I don't want to seem like someone who's just stubborn or... or crazy, you know? I've looked at all the paperwork they've shown me, and I listen to my husband when he says it's just about missed payments. I really do try to see it their way, because I want to be reasonable. 

But... I guess... it's just so hard to ignore what I've been seeing for almost two years now. It's not just one or two little things. It really feels like the bank, the loan servicer, and... and even some people at work are quietly coordinating this to push me out of my house. I know how that sounds, and I'm really sorry if it sounds unreasonable. I just... no amount of papers they show me really changes the pattern of what's been happening. 

I don't want you to think I'm inflexible, though. I'm just trying to make sense of a really confusing situation. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to be completely honest with you about where my head is at.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, related to the situation with the bank and your house?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I've never heard any voices or... or sounds that aren't there. 

I know sometimes people can experience things like that when they're under a lot of stress, or... well, I know it can happen to some people, but I promise you, nothing like that has ever happened to me. I would absolutely tell you if it did, because I want to be completely open and cooperative with you. 

Everything I've been dealing with is just based on the actual things happening around me... the paperwork and the actions I see people taking. I don't hear anything in my head or anything like that. I hope that reassures you a little bit? Like, that I'm still grounded in reality with all of this? That's a good sign, right?
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you might be misinterpreting the actions of the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job?

Um... I really, really want to say yes, because I know that's what my husband and... well, everyone else thinks. I know everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just standard paperwork and missed payments. And I try so hard to look at it that way, I really do, because I want to be agreeable and I absolutely don't want to be difficult. 

But... I just can't. Even though I want to see it your way, I know the bank, the loan servicer, and... and even those people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. It's been going on for almost two years now, and I've seen it with my own eyes. No amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing happen around me. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for, and I really don't want to disappoint you or make you think I'm just being stubborn. I just have to be honest about what I know is actually happening. Is it okay that I'm just being completely honest with you about it? I really hope you aren't upset with me.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working together against you?

I feel terrible repeating myself, because I really, really want to be helpful and give you the answer you're looking for. I want to be a good patient, I really do. But... honestly? No. I don't think I can change my mind. 

I know everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just about paperwork and missed payments. My husband, the lawyers... they all say the same thing. And I try to smile and nod because I don't want to cause trouble. But I know what's actually happening. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been living through it for almost two years now. No amount of papers they show me is going to change what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes. 

I'm really sorry... I hope you're not frustrated with me for saying that. I'm not trying to be combative, I promise. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest information I can. Is it alright that I'm standing my ground on this one? I just really want to do this right.
How often do you feel anxious or upset when thinking about the situation with the bank and your house?

Oh, um... I'm not really sure? I haven't really noticed feeling terribly upset about it, to be honest. I try so hard to just keep a positive attitude so I don't burden my husband or... or anyone else. 

I mean, I know it sounds like a lot to deal with, but I really do my best to handle it calmly. I wouldn't say I'm constantly anxious or anything like that. I don't sit around crying or panicking, I promise. I just... I keep going to work, and I make sure to keep a smile on my face. 

Is it okay that I don't have a specific amount or, like, a number of times to tell you? I just really try not to let myself get worked up, so I haven't been keeping track of anything like that. I hope that shows I'm handling things well? I really want you to see that I'm managing it all okay.
Do you think it's possible that new information could come to light that would change your mind about the bank and loan servicer working against you?

I... I really wish I could say yes, just to make everyone happy. I know it would be so much easier for my husband, and for you, if I could just say, "Oh, okay, maybe I'm wrong." I really want to be flexible, I do. 

But I just... I don't see how any new information could change anything. I know everyone keeps trying to show me these papers and saying it's just about missed payments and standard foreclosure stuff. And I've looked at them, I promise I have! I'm not trying to be difficult. But I've been living through this for almost two years. I've seen how the bank, the loan servicer, and the people at my job have been quietly working together to get me out of my house. 

No matter what new papers they might come up with, it doesn't erase what I've been seeing happen right in front of me all this time. I'm so sorry, I know that's not the answer you want. I just have to be honest about what I know is true. I hope you can understand where I'm coming from? I really don't want you to think I'm just being closed-minded.
Do you think your beliefs about the bank and loan servicer working against you could be considered a fixed part of your thinking that you cannot change, even if presented with contradictory evidence?

Oh... "fixed"... that makes it sound like I'm just being stubborn, doesn't it? I really, really don't want to come across that way to you. I pride myself on being a reasonable person, especially at my job, and I want to be a good patient for you. 

But... well, like I was trying to explain earlier, I know everyone keeps acting like this is just a normal foreclosure about missed payments and standard paperwork. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my work have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been living through it for almost two years now. 

So... I guess, if you're asking if any new papers or contradictory evidence they bring me will change my mind? No, it won't. Because no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing happen right in front of me all this time. 

I'm so sorry if that makes me sound difficult. I really don't mean to be. I just have to trust what I know is actually happening. Is it okay that I feel that way? I really hope you don't think poorly of me for saying it like that.
Do you think your beliefs about the bank and loan servicer working against you might be an exaggeration or distortion of reality?

Oh... "distortion of reality"... um, that sounds so awful, doesn't it? Like I'm completely losing my mind. I really, really hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying all this. I want so badly to just agree with you and say, "Yes, maybe I'm just exaggerating," because I know that's what everyone wants to hear. It would make everything so much easier for my husband, and probably for you, too.

But... I know I keep saying this, and I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself or being frustrating... I just can't say it's an exaggeration. I know everyone around me keeps acting like this foreclosure is just about missed payments and normal paperwork. But I know what I've been seeing for almost two years now. The bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job... they really have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I know exactly how it sounds, I really do. But it's not a distortion, it's just... it's what is actually happening to me. No amount of standard paperwork they show me changes that. I'm trying so hard to explain it right so you don't think I'm just making wild things up. Do you believe that I'm at least trying to be honest with you? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining it all, and I really hope I'm not disappointing you.
Do you think your belief about the bank and loan servicer working against you is something that might be considered unreasonable or unrealistic by others?

I... well, yes, I suppose I can see how it might look that way to other people. I really want to be fair about this, and I know how it must sound to someone who isn't living it. I mean, my husband, he definitely thinks it's unreasonable. And I hate that it causes tension between us, I really do. I want to be someone who sees things the way everyone else does. It would be so much easier.

But... I just keep coming back to the fact that everyone is acting like this foreclosure is just normal paperwork and missed payments. And I know it's not. I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been watching it happen for almost two years. 

So, yes, I know others think it's unrealistic. And I'm so sorry if that makes me seem difficult or... or like I'm not listening. I really am listening to you! I just... I can't ignore what I've been seeing, even if no one else believes me. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm just trying to be difficult on purpose. I really am trying my best to explain it so you can see where I'm coming from. Am I doing okay?
